name: encoding-base64
algorithm: Base64 (RFC 4648, standard padded alphabet) of n splitmix64 bytes, rounds times: encode, then decode back, each language's standard codec; the checksum adds per round the text length, the decoded length and one decoded byte at a moving index (README.md).

skip.c: no base64 in C's standard library
skip.rust: no base64 in Rust's std (base64 is a crate; no crate stands in)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the task has no other arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries; the round trip is tested by the lane's Go tests (TestStdEncoding_Base64Adversarial, TestStdEncoding_VectorSteps)
notes: Mk: Base64Encode into an arena reset each round (an allocation of Mk's API, counted against Mk), Base64DecodeTo into one buffer; both take the 16-byte vector path (Mula and Lemire, SSSE3 at the hosted baseline) past 32 bytes. Go: encoding/base64 Encode and Decode into buffers made once (scalar, 8 bytes a step). Zig: std.base64.standard Encoder.encode and Decoder.decode into buffers made once (scalar).
Checksums agree between Go and Mk at the quick size on the owner's machine (std-encoding session 1, 2026-11-12); the publish checksum is Go's.
Not published: no number here is a measurement.
